blocks.content: Atmospheric pressure is defined as the total weight of a column of air extending from sea level to the top of the atmosphere per unit area.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Atmospheric pressure decreases exponentially with increasing altitude due to diminishing air density.
The normal lapse rate in the troposphere is the decrease of temperature at an average rate of 6.5°C per 1,000 meters of elevation.
Temperature inversion is an atmospheric condition where warm air overlies cooler air near the surface, reversing the normal lapse rate.
Isobars are lines on a meteorological map connecting places of equal atmospheric pressure reduced to sea level.
The Earth features seven primary pressure belts influenced by atmospheric heating and rotation: Equatorial Low, two Subtropical Highs, two Subpolar Lows, and two Polar Highs.
Doldrums refer to the Equatorial Low Pressure Belt (5°N to 5°S) marked by calm winds and thermal convection.
Horse Latitudes refer to the Subtropical High Pressure Belts (30°N and 30°S) characterized by high pressure and descending air currents.
Ideal conditions for temperature inversion: long winter nights, clear skies, calm wind, and dry air near the ground.
Closely spaced isobars on a weather map indicate a steep pressure gradient force, resulting in high-speed winds.
